title: Return As Far As You Can
text:
A rabbinic parable, told to explain the prophet's call "Return to me, and I will return to you," speaks of a king whose son had gone astray. The son had drifted far from his father, in distance and in spirit, a journey of a hundred days away.

His friends urged him to go home to his father. He said he could not; the distance was too great, and he did not have the strength for the journey. He was ashamed of how far he had gone and how long he had stayed away, and the road home looked endless.

So his father, the king, sent him a message. "Return as far as you are able," he said, "and I will come to you the rest of the way."

In the same way, the parable concludes, God says to Israel, "Return to me, and I will return to you."
lesson: When a relationship is broken, do not wait for the other person to cover the whole distance. Take whatever steps you can, and go out to meet them.
